title: Weekly Scientific Lineage · 2026-W45
executive_summary:
This week's high-energy transient research establishes rigorous causal links bridging dense nuclear matter equations of state, central engine formation, relativistic jet dissipation, and early multi-messenger follow-up architectures.
- **Pulsar Surface Emission & Dense Matter Constraints**: The NICER collaboration et al. (arXiv:2610.41846) conducted comprehensive multi-wavelength pulse profile modeling from far-UV to hard X-rays on PSR J0437$-$4715, simultaneously resolving thermal surface emission and non-thermal magnetospheric power laws to measure an equatorial radius of $R_{\rm eq} = 11.35_{-0.39}^{+0.40}\,\mathrm{km}$ and mass of $M = 1.377_{-0.034}^{+0.038}\,M_\odot$, ruling out stiff equations of state with $R_{1.4} > 12.0\,\mathrm{km}$ at the $68\%$ credible level.
- **Relativistic Jets and Prompt Gamma-Ray Bursts**: The SVOM and EP teams et al. (arXiv:2610.41005) characterized GRB 241113B across $0.5\text{--}1000\,\mathrm{keV}$, establishing that its soft prompt spectrum ($E_{\rm peak}^{\rm obs} \approx 35\text{--}37\,\mathrm{keV}$) arises from intrinsic jet dissipation with bulk Lorentz factor $\Gamma_0 > 100$ decelerating into a stellar wind ($s=2$), definitively excluding shock breakout and dirty-fireball baryonic loading scenarios.
- **Multi-Messenger Gravitational-Wave Follow-up**: The Deep Synoptic Array collaboration et al. (arXiv:2610.40958) developed a reinforcement-learning-guided rapid slewing policy capturing up to $75\%\text{--}90\%$ of immediate binary neutron star coalescences down to coherent radio fluences of $20\,\mathrm{mJy\,ms}$, probing prompt radio emission fractions down to $10^{-13}\text{--}10^{-10}$ of available central engine energy reservoirs.
- **Compact Remnant Microphysics and Nucleosynthesis**: Zhu et al. (arXiv:2610.40907) showed via comprehensive network calculations that $^{250}\mathrm{Cm}$ dominates the $0.2\text{--}5\,\mathrm{MeV}$ $\gamma$-ray line flux of strong $r$-process remnants from $2{,}000$ to $20{,}000\,\mathrm{yr}$ post-merger, providing an unambiguous actinide nucleosynthetic tracer, while Caplan et al. (arXiv:2610.40892) demonstrated via molecular dynamics that static shear strain exponentially enhances defect-mediated diffusion in crustal Yukawa lattices.
- **Dynamical Transients and Binary Coalescence Populations**: Zevin et al. (arXiv:2610.40782) resolved the apparent age tension of GW170817 by finding that empirical delay-time distributions favor extended delays ($t_{\rm min} > 7.5\,\mathrm{Gyr}$), while Grishin et al. (arXiv:2610.40767) demonstrated that chaotic diving orbits in flattened nuclear potentials boost tidal disruption rates by $\sim 10\times$ above standard two-body loss-cone limits.

overview_matrix.domain: Pulsar Electrodynamics & Dense Matter Equations of State
overview_matrix.key_question: How can multi-wavelength pulse profile modeling eliminate degeneracies between warm surface emission, heated magnetic polar caps, and non-thermal magnetospheric power laws to robustly constrain neutron star radii?
overview_matrix.core_findings: - [arXiv:2610.41846] (The NICER collaboration et al.): Coupled $2.56\,\mathrm{Ms}$ of NICER timing, XMM-Newton, NuSTAR hard X-ray ($3\text{--}16\,\mathrm{keV}$), and HST far-UV spectroscopy to measure $R_{\rm eq} = 11.35_{-0.39}^{+0.40}\,\mathrm{km}$ and $M = 1.377_{-0.034}^{+0.038}\,M_\odot$ for PSR J0437$-$4715, strictly ruling out stiff nuclear matter equations of state with $R_{1.4} > 12.0\,\mathrm{km}$ at the $68\%$ credibility level.
overview_matrix.significance: Demonstrates that spanning far-UV to hard X-rays isolates the whole-surface temperature ($T_{\rm else} = (2.82 \pm 0.05) \times 10^{5}\,\mathrm{K}$) and magnetospheric index ($\Gamma_{\rm PL} = 1.310_{-0.061}^{+0.054}$), shrinking systematic radius uncertainties to below $400\,\mathrm{m}$.

overview_matrix.key_question: What is the physical mechanism underpinning prompt spectral softness in X-ray rich bursts and X-ray flashes: viewing geometry, low Lorentz factor baryon loading, shock breakout, or intrinsic jet dissipation?
overview_matrix.core_findings: - [arXiv:2610.41005] (The SVOM and EP teams et al.): Discovered GRB 241113B as an on-axis soft burst ($E_{\rm peak}^{\rm obs} \approx 35\text{--}37\,\mathrm{keV}$) whose early deceleration peak ($t_b \approx 263\,\mathrm{s}$) and afterglow forward shock modeling require a high bulk Lorentz factor ($\Gamma_0 > 100$, posterior bounds $125\text{--}263$) expanding into a wind medium ($s=2$), ruling out shock breakout and dirty fireballs.
overview_matrix.significance: Proves that extreme prompt softness can originate intrinsically from dissipative internal shocks or magnetic reconnection in ultra-relativistic jets rather than heavy baryonic loading or viewing angle effects.

overview_matrix.domain: Prompt Gravitational-Wave Radio Counterparts & Multi-Messenger Search
overview_matrix.key_question: Can high-speed autonomous slewing and real-time beamforming capture sub-second coherent radio bursts from compact binary coalescences under dynamic early-warning localization uncertainty?
overview_matrix.core_findings:
- [arXiv:2610.40958] (The DSA collaboration et al.): Formulated a Markov Decision Process slewing policy with the Deep Synoptic Array achieving $75\%\text{--}90\%$ capture rates for visible BNS mergers down to $20\,\mathrm{mJy\,ms}$, probing coherent radio burst efficiencies of $E_{\rm radio}/E_{\rm engine} \sim 10^{-13}\text{--}10^{-10}$.
- [arXiv:2610.41119] (Zhang et al.): Constructed MAGIKS, a multimodal contrastive and cross-attentive architecture conditioned on dynamic ejecta parameters, improving kilonova identification recall from $4.8\%$ (optical alone) to $39.8\%$ within candidate galleries of 5000 contaminants.
overview_matrix.significance: Establishes a quantitative blueprint for capturing prompt coherent emission seconds before and after compact mergers while overcoming optical follow-up contamination.

overview_matrix.domain: Dense Stellar Remnants: Microphysics, Explosions & Remnants
overview_matrix.key_question: How do non-ideal microphysical processes—such as lattice strain, quark-hadron phase transitions, and actinide decay—shape compact star structure, supernova explosion dynamics, and remnant observables?
overview_matrix.core_findings:
- [arXiv:2610.40907] (Zhu et al.): Modeled late-time secular equilibrium nucleosynthesis to reveal that $^{250}\mathrm{Cm}$ ($\tau_{1/2} \approx 8300\,\mathrm{yr}$) accounts for $67\%\text{--}87\%$ of the $0.2\text{--}5\,\mathrm{MeV}$ line luminosity in aged $r$-process remnants via emission lines at $989\,\mathrm{keV}$, $1032\,\mathrm{keV}$, and $1079\,\mathrm{keV}$.
- [arXiv:2610.40892] (Caplan et al.): Used molecular dynamics to demonstrate that static shear strain $\varepsilon$ lowers the Frenkel pair nucleation barrier across an activation volume of $N_{\rm act} \approx 31$ ions, exponentially amplifying self-diffusion in neutron star crusts.
- [arXiv:2610.41242] (Kuroda et al.): Simulated general-relativistic core-collapse with hybrid EOSs, showing that quark-hadron phase transitions launch a second shock that concentrates remnant gravitational masses into high-mass peaks at $\sim 1.70\,M_\odot$ by anti-correlating collapse delay with progenitor compactness $\xi_{1.75}$.
overview_matrix.significance: Connects microscopic lattice transport and nuclear reaction channels directly to macroscopic observable phenomena including remnant gamma-ray spectra, magnetic field decay timescales, and mass distribution peaks.

overview_matrix.domain: Binary Black Hole & Loss-Cone Dynamics in Galactic Nuclei
overview_matrix.key_question: How do non-spherical potential perturbations, gas migration in AGN accretion disks, and detector selection biases alter the merger rates and parameter inferences of compact binaries?
overview_matrix.core_findings:
- [arXiv:2610.40767] (Grishin et al.): Solved a 2D equilibrium Fokker-Planck equation coupling chaotic diving orbits to find that tidal disruption rates in flattened galactic potentials are enhanced by $\Gamma/\Gamma_{\rm cl} \approx 1 + \ln(j_d/j_t)$, yielding a $\sim 10\times$ enhancement over standard two-body relaxation.
- [arXiv:2610.40774] (Fairhurst et al.): Demonstrated that joint $(\chi_{\rm eff}, \chi_{\rm p})$ likelihood ratio tests improve hierarchical merger classification to $35\%$ and showed that asymmetric mass ratios ($q \lesssim 0.4$) dramatically elevate spin precession measurability.
- [arXiv:2610.40787] (Santini et al.): Modeled BBH migration within cosmological AGN disk models, proving that local merger rate densities are highly sensitive to Shakura-Sunyaev viscosity (peaking at $280\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ for $\alpha=0.01$ vs. $0.5\text{--}6\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ for $\alpha=0.1$).
overview_matrix.significance: Reveals how circum-nuclear geometry, chaotic orbital dynamics, and disk-gas drag systematically boost compact object interaction rates and shape gravitational-wave population distributions.

thematic_highlights.summary: By integrating $2.56\,\mathrm{Ms}$ of NICER timing, XMM-Newton EPIC MOS, NuSTAR hard X-ray ($3\text{--}16\,\mathrm{keV}$), and HST STIS far-UV spectroscopy ($1150\text{--}1700\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$), the NICER collaboration (arXiv:2610.41846) achieved a definitive radius measurement for the nearby millisecond pulsar PSR J0437$-$4715 ($R_{\rm eq} = 11.35_{-0.39}^{+0.40}\,\mathrm{km}$, $M = 1.377_{-0.034}^{+0.038}\,M_\odot$). papers.problem: Optimizing slewing and pointing schedules for single-pointing array telescopes (DSA) under rapidly evolving, uncertain gravitational-wave early-warning localization maps to capture millisecond-duration prompt coherent radio bursts around compact binary coalescences.

papers.title: GRB 241113B: the first SVOM and EP gamma-ray burst A soft GRB likely seen on-axis, from soft X-rays to gamma-rays
papers.result:
GRB 241113B is confirmed as an intrinsically soft Type II GRB (XRR/XRF) observed on-axis within a redshift range $0.5 \lesssim z \lesssim 3.5$. Joint prompt spectral fitting favors a cutoff power-law (CPL) model with photon index $\alpha = -1.80^{+0.16}_{-0.10}$ and $E^{\mathrm{obs}}_{\mathrm{peak}} \approx 35	ext{--}37	ext{ keV}$. The prompt duration follows an energy-dependent scaling law $\log T_{90} = \alpha \log(E/50\,\mathrm{keV}) + \log K_{50}$ with $\alpha = -0.35^{+0.10}_{-0.06}$ ($K_{50} = 54.2^{+2.8}_{-4.2}$). The early multiband afterglow peaks at deceleration time $t_b = 263^{+68}_{-91}\,\mathrm{s}$ and decays with $\alpha_2 = -1.40^{+0.03}_{-0.04}$ and spectral index $ eta_{\mathrm{OX}} = 0.66^{+0.04}_{-0.03}$. VegasAfterglow modeling confirms a relativistic top-hat jet propagating into a wind-like circumstellar medium ($s=2$) in the slow cooling regime ($
u_m < 
u_{\mathrm{opt}} < 
u_{\mathrm{X}} < 
u_c$) with electron index $p = 2.31 \pm 0.08$. The bulk Lorentz factor is constrained to $\Gamma_0 > 100$ (posterior bounds $\Gamma_0 \sim 125	ext{--}263$), ruling out both shock breakout (SBO) and high baryon loading (dirty fireball) scenarios.
papers.problem: Unveiling the physical origin of prompt spectral softness in X-ray rich bursts (XRR) and X-ray flashes (XRF): whether they are driven by geometric viewing angle effects (off-axis jets), relativistic shock breakouts, dirty fireballs with heavy baryon loading ($\Gamma_0 \ll 100$), or intrinsic jet dissipative processes.
papers.method: Joint prompt spectral fitting across 0.5–1000 keV combining EP/WXT, SVOM/ECLAIRs, and SVOM/GRM with PL, CPL, and Band models. Phenomenological smoothly broken power-law (SBPL) and forward shock Bayesian numerical inference using VegasAfterglow were applied to X-ray (EP/FXT, Swift/XRT) and optical (KAIT, SVOM/VT) light curves, comparing constant ISM vs. wind-like circumstellar density profiles.
papers.reason: This is the first joint detection of a gamma-ray burst (GRB 241113B) by both SVOM and Einstein Probe, bridging the gap between soft X-ray transients and classic GRBs with high-precision broadband spectro-temporal modeling.

papers.title: A multi-wavelength view of PSR J0437-4715 with NICER and other missions: Radius measurements from far-ultraviolet to hard X-ray pulse profile modeling
papers.result: Using the ST+PDT+EL+PL surface emission configuration, the headline PPM inference yields an equatorial radius of $R_{\rm eq} = 11.35_{-0.39}^{+0.40}\,\mathrm{km}$ (or $R_{\rm eq} = 11.345_{-0.388}^{+0.399}\,\mathrm{km}$) and a mass of $M = 1.377_{-0.034}^{+0.038}\,M_{\odot}$. The whole-surface warm emission has an effective temperature in the stellar frame of $\log_{10}(T_{\rm else}\,[\mathrm{K}]) = 5.451 \pm 0.008$ ($T_{\rm else} = (2.82 \pm 0.05) \times 10^{5}\,\mathrm{K}$), translating to an observer at infinity to $T_{\rm else}^{\infty} = T_{\rm else}/(1+z) = (2.26 \pm 0.03) \times 10^{5}\,\mathrm{K}$ via the gravitational redshift $1+z = \left(1 - \frac{2GM}{R_{\rm eq}c^2}\right)^{-1/2}$, with observed flux scaling as $F \propto (R_{\rm eq}^{\infty}/d)^2 \sigma (T_{\rm else}^{\infty})^4$. The pulsed non-thermal power-law component exhibits photon index $\Gamma_{\rm PL} = 1.310_{-0.061}^{+0.054}$ and pulsed amplitude $A_{\rm PL} = 0.684_{-0.057}^{+0.059}$. At the 95% credibility level, the upper limit of the neutron star radius is reduced by $\approx 0.4\text{--}0.6\,\mathrm{km}$, yielding inferred radius at $1.4\,M_{\odot}$ of $R_{1.4} = 11.52_{-0.50}^{+0.66}\,\mathrm{km}$ (piecewise polytrope) and $11.48_{-0.52}^{+0.61}\,\mathrm{km}$ (speed of sound), ruling out stiff EOSs with $R > 12.0\,\mathrm{km}$ at 68% credibility.
papers.problem: Previous radius inferences of PSR J0437-4715 suffered from strong degeneracies between the pulsed non-thermal magnetospheric power-law tail, the soft thermal hot spots, and the diffuse warm stellar surface. Without joint far-UV (HST) and hard X-ray (NuSTAR) coverage, the non-thermal normalization and whole-surface emission were unconstrained, leading to divergent radius posteriors ranging from $\sim 7.9\,\mathrm{km}$ up to $\sim 14.1\,\mathrm{km}$.
papers.method: The authors perform multi-wavelength pulse profile modeling within an extended X-PSI Bayesian inference framework over $0.007\text{--}16.0\,\mathrm{keV}$, integrating $2.56\,\mathrm{Ms}$ of NICER XTI data, $113\,\mathrm{ks}$ of XMM-Newton EPIC MOS data, $221\,\mathrm{ks}$ of NuSTAR FPM data ($3.0\text{--}16.0\,\mathrm{keV}$), and HST STIS far-UV spectroscopy ($1150\text{--}1700\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$). The likelihood couples a modified Gaussian log-likelihood for HST STIS fluxes $\mathcal{L}(\theta,\mathbf{B})=\sum_{i,k}\left[\frac{(c_{ik}(\theta)-d_{ik}+B_{i}T_{\rm exp}\int_{\phi_{k}}d\phi)^2}{\sigma_{ik}^2}+\ln(2\pi\sigma_{ik}^2)\right]$ with Poisson likelihoods for X-ray timing data. The geometric model combines a northern single-temperature (ST) hydrogen atmosphere spot (NSXH), an equatorial/southern protruding dual-temperature (PDT) spot, an unheated warm surface (EL) with partially ionized hydrogen (NSXHp), and an observer-frame sinusoidally modulated power law $F(E,\phi)=N_{\mathrm{PL}}(E/1\,\mathrm{keV})^{-\Gamma_{\mathrm{PL}}}[1+A_{\mathrm{PL}}\cos(2\pi(\phi-\phi_{\mathrm{PL}}))]$ evaluated using MultiNest nested sampling.
papers.reason: This work performs an unprecedented multi-wavelength pulse profile modeling (PPM) of the nearest millisecond pulsar PSR J0437-4715 combining HST, NICER, XMM-Newton, and NuSTAR datasets to obtain the tightest neutron star radius and equation of state constraints to date.

papers.title: Chaos and loss: reevaluating the loss-cone formalism in the context of chaotic diving orbits in flattened potentials
papers.result: Disruption rates in flattened potentials are enhanced over the classical loss-cone rate $\Gamma_{\rm cl}$ by a multiplicative factor $\Gamma / \Gamma_{\rm cl} \approx 1 + \ln(j_d / j_t)$, typically yielding an order-of-magnitude increase ($\sim 10\times$) for characteristic chaotic diving thresholds $j_d \gtrsim 0.1$. When diffusion is weak ($\sigma \lesssim 0.1 j_t$), disruptions are highly anisotropic and aligned near the disk plane ($|\cos i| \to 1$), while in the well-mixed regime ($\sigma \gtrsim j_t$), the penetration factor distribution follows $p(\beta) \propto \beta^{-2}$.
papers.problem: Classical loss-cone theory based solely on two-body relaxation underestimates disruption rates by omitting chaotic orbit migration, whereas previous collisionless chaotic models neglected depletion of the diving region and diffusion coupling, hindering self-consistent equilibrium predictions.
papers.method: The authors construct a 2D equilibrium Fokker-Planck model $p(j_z, j)$ coupling two-body scattering, rapid uniform chaotic redistribution within diving orbits ($j < j_d$), and pericenter loss ($j < j_t$), supplemented by 1D/2D analytical Bessel solutions and walker-based Monte Carlo simulations.
papers.reason: The paper provides an improved theoretical framework combining two-body diffusion and collisionless chaotic diving orbits in flattened galactic potentials, yielding a key boost factor $1 + \ln(j_d/j_t)$ to tidal disruption event (TDE) rates.

papers.title: Surprisingly normal? GW241011 and GW241110 in the context of hierarchical merger classification
papers.result: Hierarchical mergers (1G+2G) are classified via likelihood ratio metrics: in simulated realistic cluster (CMC) mergers, the $\chi_{\mathrm{p}}$ metric alone achieves a $24\%$ ($182$ events) classification rate, whereas a joint $(\chi_{\mathrm{eff}}, \chi_{\mathrm{p}})$ metric increases identification to $35\%$ ($265$ events) by eliminating face-on selection vulnerability. Binary mass ratio $q$ is identified as the dominant intrinsic driver of identification over primary mass $m_{1,\mathrm{det}}$, with unequal-mass binaries ($q \lesssim 0.4$) dramatically improving precession measurement precision.
papers.problem: Whether low-mass, highly spinning precessing black hole merger candidates such as GW241011 and GW241110 represent an unexpected subpopulation of hierarchical mergers or naturally emerge when detector selection effects and spin measurability are taken into account.
papers.method: The authors perform Bilby/Dynesty Bayesian parameter estimation on grid injections ($m_{1,\mathrm{det}} \in [10, 120]\,M_\odot$, $a_1=0.7, a_2=0$, $\mathrm{SNR}=12, 30$) and CMC globular cluster populations weighted by the Madau-Dickinson cluster formation rate $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{GC}}(z) \propto \frac{(1+z)^\lambda}{1+\left[(1+z)/(1+z_p)\right]^{\lambda+\kappa}}$ ($\ ext{with } \lambda=2.6, \kappa=3.6, z_p=2.2$), evaluating classification performance via one-dimensional $\mathrm{LR}_{p}$ and joint $(\chi_{\mathrm{eff}}, \chi_{\mathrm{p}})$ likelihood ratios.
papers.reason: This paper investigates whether low-mass binary black hole events like GW241011 and GW241110 are naturally expected within hierarchical merger channels and formulates likelihood-ratio classification metrics across spin-precession parameter space.

papers.title: Missing Mergers: On the Unexpected Delay-Time Distribution of Binary Neutron Star Mergers
papers.result: The stellar population analysis of NGC 4993 yields a mass-weighted age of $12.4^{+0.5}_{-0.7}\,\mathrm{Gyr}$. Under an efficiency-normalized power-law DTD model ($\mathrm{DTD} = A t^{\alpha}$), the minimum delay time is constrained to $t_{\rm min} > 7.5\pm 0.2\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ (90% credible level) and $t_{\rm min} > 5.6\pm 0.2\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ (95% credible level), peaking at $12.6\pm 0.7\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ for $\alpha = -1$. The empirical $(12.6\,\mathrm{Gyr}, -1)$ model is favored over the canonical $(10\,\mathrm{Myr}, -1)$ model by a Bayes/likelihood factor of 41–138.
papers.problem: Standard binary neutron star evolution predicts a delay-time distribution $dN/dt \propto t^{-1}$ with $t_{\rm min} \sim 10\,\mathrm{Myr}$, implying that short-delay mergers should outnumber long-delay mergers by $\sim 16:1$, creating a severe statistical tension with GW170817 originating in an extremely old stellar population.
papers.method: The host galaxy NGC 4993 was analyzed using prospector and FSPS with MIST isochrones and MILES spectral libraries across 14 photometric bands and VLT/MUSE integral field spectroscopy to reconstruct its non-parametric star formation history (SFH). Poisson likelihood frameworks incorporating cosmic star formation history $\psi(t)$ and DTD parameterizations ($A t^\alpha$) were evaluated via nested sampling with dynesty.
papers.reason: The study directly constrains the delay-time distribution (DTD) of binary neutron star mergers, showing an unexpected preference for multi-Gyr delay times that challenges standard isolated binary evolution models and impacts kilonova and short gamma-ray burst progenitor rates.

papers.title: Cosmic merger rates and population evolution of binary black hole mergers in AGN disks
papers.result: The local comoving merger rate density is primarily governed by the disk viscosity parameter $\alpha$: at $z=0.2$, $\mathcal{R}(z=0.2)=24^{+13}_{-8}\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ for $\alpha=0.01$ (peaking at $z\simeq 1.8$ at $280^{+170}_{-110}\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$), whereas $\alpha=0.1$ reduces the rates by roughly an order of magnitude to $0.5\text{--}6\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ ($f_{\mathrm{AGN}}\sim 2\%\text{--}38\%$), making $\alpha=0.1$ consistent with empirical electromagnetic flare upper limits ($f_{\mathrm{AGN}}\lesssim 40\%$). For the Einstein Telescope ($T_{\mathrm{obs}}=1\,\mathrm{yr}$, SNR $\rho>12$), expected detections reach $0.9\text{--}1.6\times 10^5$ events for $\alpha=0.01$ and $\sim 10^4$ for $\alpha=0.1$, with super-Eddington models (CAT-SE) predicting persistent detections out to $z\simeq 8$.
papers.problem: Current ground-based gravitational wave detectors only observe stellar-mass BBH mergers out to $z\sim 1.5$, leaving the high-redshift ($z\gtrsim 2\text{--}10$) evolution of BBH merger rates, their connection to SMBH accretion pathways (Eddington-limited vs. super-Eddington), and the fraction of LVK mergers produced in AGN disks unconstrained.
papers.method: The ARISE framework couples a semi-analytic AGN disk dynamical model (FastClusterAGN accounting for Type I/II migration, gas damping, pairing with semi-major axis distribution $p(a)\propto a^{9/2}$, and gravitational wave hardening) with cosmological semi-analytic models of SMBH growth (CAT-EL and CAT-SE). Source-frame merger rate densities $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{AGN}}(z)$ are computed by integrating the mean galaxy merger rate $\bar{\Gamma}$ weighted by the comoving active AGN number density $n_{\mathrm{AGN}}(z)$ and active fraction $f_{\mathrm{active}}(M_\bullet, z)=\frac{\int_{\dot{M}_{\bullet,\mathrm{min}}}^\infty d\dot{M}_\bullet\,\Phi}{\int_0^\infty d\dot{M}_\bullet\,\Phi}$.
papers.reason: This work develops the ARISE framework linking binary black hole (BBH) mergers in AGN disks to cosmological AGN and SMBH growth, providing testable merger rates and population predictions for current LVK observations and next-generation gravitational wave detectors like the Einstein Telescope.

papers.title: How to feed your dragon: the role of turbulence in AGN activity
papers.result: Turbulence plays a dual role by driving gas into the central accretion region and providing low-density channels for outward jet breakout. Without turbulence ($\mathfrak{M}=0$), self-limiting accretion confines jet power to $\le 10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ (dropping to $<10^{37}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$), whereas supersonic turbulence ($\mathfrak{M}=4$) sustains median jet powers of $10^{40}\text{--}10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, reproducing FR0-like Eddington ratios $L_{\rm jet}/L_{\rm Edd}$. For low efficiencies $\varepsilon$, jet power scales linearly with $\varepsilon$, while exceeding $\varepsilon > 10^{-1}$ leads to strong self-limiting accretion by expelling central gas reservoirs.
papers.problem: How interstellar medium (ISM) turbulence regulates both the fueling of supermassive black hole accretion and the confinement or breakout of self-consistently launched AGN jets, resolving the severe shut-off of cold accretion observed in quiescent/uniform media.
papers.method: 3D hydrodynamic simulations using the moving-mesh code Arepo in a $(2\,\mathrm{kpc})^3$ box with turbulent driving characterized by specific energy injection rate $\epsilon = \alpha \cdot \frac{c_{s}^3}{2^3 \cdot l}$ across Mach numbers $\mathfrak{M} \in \{0.5, 1, 2, 4\}$. Jets are launched self-consistently via Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion: $\dot{M}_{\mathrm{BHL}}=\frac{4\pi\langle\rho\rangle G^{2}M^{2}_{\mathrm{BH}}}{(\langle c_{s}\rangle^{2}+\langle v_{\mathrm{gas}}\rangle^{2})^{3/2}}$ with power $L_{\mathrm{jet}}=\varepsilon_{t}(t)\dot{M}_{\mathrm{BHL}}c^{2}$.
papers.reason: The paper studies accretion-regulated AGN jet feedback and propagation in turbulent multiphase ISM using Arepo simulations, establishing scaling relations between jet power, turbulence Mach number, and efficiency factor, which is physically relevant to relativistic jet propagation and compact radio environments (FR0s).

papers.title: Stress-enhanced diffusion in Yukawa crystals
papers.result: Static shear strain $\varepsilon$ exponentially enhances self-diffusion by lowering the activation energy barrier for Frenkel defect pair formation via the stored elastic strain energy $\sigma = \frac{1}{2}\mu\varepsilon^2$ within an activation volume $V^*$ containing $N_{\rm act} \equiv n_i V^* \approx 31 \pm 1$ ions across astrophysically relevant screenings ($\kappa \lesssim 1$). The modified diffusion coefficient follows $D(\Gamma^*,\varepsilon) = D_0(\Gamma^*) \exp\left[\frac{1}{2} N_{\rm act} \tilde{\mu} \Gamma \varepsilon^2\right]$, which scales near melting as $D(\Gamma^*,\varepsilon) = \frac{787}{\Gamma^*} \exp\left[-\left(20 - 5\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{0.1}\right)^2\right)\Gamma^*\right]$, increasing diffusion by orders of magnitude at high coupling $\Gamma^*$.
papers.problem: Understanding whether and how static elastic shear stress alters self-diffusion in body-centered cubic (bcc) Yukawa crystals relevant to neutron star crusts and white dwarf interiors, specifically differentiating whether strain modifies defect migration mobility or defect pair nucleation rates.
papers.method: Performed classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of bcc Yukawa crystals with frozen boundary layers under static $xy$-shear strain using LAMMPS, tracking ion mean-squared displacements (MSDs) across various coupling parameters $\Gamma^*$ and screening parameters $\kappa$ to extract defect nucleation rates $\nu(\varepsilon)$ and activation volumes $V^*$.
papers.reason: This work quantitatively establishes how static shear strains exponentially accelerate self-diffusion in Yukawa crystals via Frenkel pair nucleation, providing key microphysical inputs for magnetar crustal creep, stress relaxation, and burst trigger mechanics.

papers.title: The Importance of Curium-250 to the $γ$-Ray Signature of $r$-Process Remnants
papers.result: In strong $r$-process ejecta, $^{250}\mathrm{Cm}$ achieves a mass fraction $\gtrapprox 0.2\%$ (up to $2.0\%$) and dominates the $0.2 - 5\ \mathrm{MeV}$ $\gamma$-ray photon budget at $t \sim 2{,}000 - 20{,}000\ \mathrm{yr}$ with peak emission fractions of $67\% - 87\%$. With a total half-life $\tau_{1/2} \approx 8300\ \mathrm{yr}$ governed by spontaneous fission, $\alpha$-, and $\beta^-$-decay, the incident energy line flux scales as $F_{\gamma}(t) = \frac{M_{\mathrm{Cm}} E_{\gamma} R_{\gamma}(t)}{4\pi D^2}$, yielding prominent diagnostic lines including $^{250}\mathrm{Bk}$ ($989, 1032\ \mathrm{keV}$), $^{246\mathrm{m}}\mathrm{Am}$ ($1079\ \mathrm{keV}$), and fission product $^{140}\mathrm{La}$ ($1596\ \mathrm{keV}$).
papers.problem: Identifying unambiguous, long-lived electromagnetic signatures of heavy actinide nucleosynthesis in aging supernova or neutron star merger remnants to confirm the occurrence of a strong $r$-process.
papers.method: Performed $15{,}625$ nucleosynthesis simulations using the PRISM reaction network across parameter space ($\rho_0 \in [10^6, 10^{9.5}]\ \mathrm{g\ cm^{-3}}$, $\tau \in [10^{-3.6}, 10^{-1}]\ \mathrm{s}$, $Y_e \in [0.005, 0.5]$), combined with the GEF fission code and late-time secular equilibrium gamma-ray spectral modeling $S^\gamma(E, t) = \sum F(t) S^\gamma(E)$.
papers.reason: The paper identifies $^{250}\mathrm{Cm}$ as the primary gamma-ray emitter in strong $r$-process remnants at ages of $2{,}000 - 20{,}000\ \mathrm{yr}$, providing crucial diagnostic line predictions for high-energy remnant observations.

papers.title: Two-Fluid Radial Stability of Dark-Matter-Admixed Compact Objects: Dark Compact Planets, Dark White Dwarfs, Dark Neutron Stars, and Dark Oysters
papers.result: Dynamic radial stability is strictly governed by the fundamental mode frequency $\omega_0^2 > 0$. Strong repulsive self-interaction ($y=10^3$) yields a stiffer dark matter equation of state that supports extended dark halos around compact ordinary matter cores, with maximum stable masses scaling as $M_{\rm max} \propto m_f^{-2}$, reaching up to $66.79 M_\odot$ for $m_f = 2\ \mathrm{GeV}$, $10.69 M_\odot$ for $m_f = 5\ \mathrm{GeV}$, and $2.672 M_\odot$ for $m_f = 10\ \mathrm{GeV}$. The gravitational redshift at the visible ordinary matter surface is given by $1+z_{\mathrm{OM}} = e^{\Delta\Phi_{\rm halo}}/\sqrt{1-2M/R}$ where $\Delta\Phi_{\rm halo} = \int_{R_{\mathrm{OM}}}^{R}[m(r)+4\pi r^{3}p(r)]/[r(r-2m(r))]\,\mathrm{d}r$, allowing stable configurations to exceed the standard vacuum Buchdahl redshift limit ($z=2$).
papers.problem: Static turning-point criteria based on Jacobian determinants $J \equiv \det[\partial(N_{\rm OM},N_{\rm DM})/\partial(p_{\rm OM}^c,p_{\rm DM}^c)]=0$ do not distinguish fundamental radial instability from overtone zero-crossings, risking misclassification of dynamically unstable two-fluid compact stars as stable.
papers.method: Coupled two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) equations and two-fluid relativistic radial pulsation equations are solved dynamically across central pressures $(p_{\rm OM}^c, p_{\rm DM}^c)$. Ordinary matter is described by unified EOS (BPS, Negele-Vautherin, and Annala et al. EoS-I / Chandrasekhar EOS) and dark matter by self-repulsive degenerate Fermi gas models parameterized by fermion mass $m_f \in \{2, 5, 10, 100\}\ \mathrm{GeV}$ and interaction parameter $y \in \{0.1, 10^3\}$.
papers.reason: The paper conducts a rigorous two-fluid relativistic radial stability analysis of dark-matter-admixed compact objects (DCPs, DWDs, DNSs, and dark oysters) across wide parameter spaces, demonstrating that static turning points fail to distinguish higher-overtone zeros and identifying high-redshift ($z_{\rm OM} > 2$) signatures relevant for compact object structure and lensing limits.

papers.title: MAGIKS: Multimodal Alignment and Gravitational-Wave-Conditioned Interaction for Kilonova Search
papers.result: In candidate galleries containing 5000 transients, MAGIKS achieves a Recall@1 of $39.8\%$ (compared to $4.8\%$ for optical-only and $0.2\%$ for sky-localization-only baselines) and an MRR of $0.488$; for GW170817 under Rubin observing conditions, Recall@1 reaches $87.3\%$ and Recall@10 reaches $95.7\%$, while pairwise binary classification yields an AUROC of $0.983$ and an accuracy of $0.942$.
papers.problem: Wide-field optical searches following GW triggers (BNS and NSBH mergers) are heavily contaminated by thousands of spatio-temporally compatible non-kilonova transients (e.g., SNe, AGNs, TDEs), where pure optical classification or spatial sky-map priors alone fail to jointly assess physical consistency.
papers.method: An align-before-fuse multimodal architecture that combines a GW encoder (MLP for 7 scalar parameters including $\mathcal{M}_c^{\rm det}$, spins, $\cos\iota$, and $d_L$, plus a 1D-CNN for 3D sky maps) and an optical encoder (modified mTAN with SNR-biased attention for irregular multiband light curves), pre-aligned via time-aware contrastive loss and fused via dual cross-attention conditioned on physical ejecta properties $\bm{\psi} = (\log_{10}(M_{\rm dyn}/M_\odot), \log_{10}(M_{\rm wind}/M_\odot), |\cos\iota|, \log_{10}(d_L/\mathrm{Gpc}))$.
papers.reason: It addresses the rapid identification and ranking of kilonova counterparts to gravitational-wave (GW) triggers in large-scale optical surveys like Vera C. Rubin/LSST, directly serving compact object multimessenger follow-up.

papers.title: Effect of quark-hadron phase transitions on the neutron star mass distribution
papers.result: The phase transition triggers a second collapse and shock wave, with the delay time $\Delta t_{\mathrm{collapse}}$ anti-correlating with progenitor compactness $\xi_{1.75}$. Lower-compactness progenitors accrete longer before reaching the PT onset density, leaving heavier remnants and naturally concentrating neutron star gravitational masses into narrow high-mass peaks at $\sim 1.70\,M_\odot$ (RDF1.1, ranging $1.66\text{--}1.72\,M_\odot$) or $1.55\text{--}1.70\,M_\odot$ (RDF1.2). The critical compactness dividing explosion from black hole formation is $\xi_{1.75} \sim 0.59\text{--}0.69$ for RDF1.1 and $\sim 1.04\text{--}1.07$ for RDF1.2.
papers.problem: Observed neutron star mass distributions show a bimodal structure with a high-mass peak around $1.75\text{--}1.8\,M_\odot$, which standard neutrino-driven core-collapse supernova simulations typically fail to reproduce because high-compactness progenitors usually collapse directly into black holes rather than exploding.
papers.method: Performed systematic 1D general-relativistic hydrodynamic simulations using the `GR1D` code with M1 neutrino transport across solar-metallicity progenitors ($13\text{--}120\,M_\odot$, with step $\Delta M = 0.2\,M_\odot$ for $13\text{--}30\,M_\odot$). Used hybrid equations of state (RDF1.1 and RDF1.2) combining DD2 with a relativistic density functional quark model with onset thresholds $\rho_{\mathrm{onset}} \approx 4.07 \times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ ($M_{\mathrm{onset}} \approx 1.60\,M_\odot$) and $\rho_{\mathrm{onset}} \approx 3.15 \times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ ($M_{\mathrm{onset}} \approx 1.44\,M_\odot$). Compactness was defined via $\xi_M = \frac{M / M_\odot}{R(M_{\mathrm{bary}} = M) / (1000\,\mathrm{km})}$.
papers.reason: This work explores how a first-order quark-hadron phase transition (PT) in core-collapse supernovae naturally generates the observed high-mass peak ($1.55\text{--}1.72\,M_\odot$) of neutron stars through accretion delay before the second collapse.

papers.title: Enhanced Detectability of Very-High-Energy Gamma Rays from Off-Axis Short Gamma-Ray Bursts: Impacts of Structured Jets and External Inverse-Compton Scattering
papers.result: Structured jets (Gaussian and power-law) yield much stronger off-axis $1\,\mathrm{TeV}$ EIC emission than top-hat jets due to relativistic beaming and lateral energy profiles. In the coasting phase with constant seed photon luminosity, the EIC flux scales as $F_{\varepsilon}^{\rm EIC} \propto T$ in the Thomson regime for $\varepsilon_m^{\rm EIC} < \varepsilon < \varepsilon_c^{\rm EIC}$, and rapidly decays as $F_{\varepsilon}^{\rm EIC} \propto T^{-33/7}$ at $T \gtrsim T_a \sim 300\,\mathrm{s}$, whereas synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) emission rises sharply as $F_{\varepsilon}^{\rm SSC} \propto T^4$ before dominating after the deceleration stage ($T \sim 5 \times 10^3\,\mathrm{s}$).
papers.problem: Whether off-axis short GRBs can produce detectable VHE gamma rays via EIC scattering of extended emission, X-ray plateau, or kilonova seed photons within realistic structured jet geometries.
papers.method: Numerical modeling using the AMES code integrating emissions over equal-arrival-time surfaces, incorporating Klein-Nishina suppression, forward shock relativistic electron dynamics, and external seed photon fields characterized by broken power-law spectra ($G(\varepsilon)$ with break $\varepsilon_b = E_b / \Gamma$, $\beta_1 = 0.5$, $\beta_2 = 2.0$) and temporal luminosity decay $L(T) \propto T^{-\alpha}$.
papers.reason: The study demonstrates that structured jets substantially enhance off-axis very-high-energy (VHE) external inverse-Compton (EIC) emission from short GRBs compared to top-hat jets, offering critical multi-messenger detection prospects for CTAO and gravitational wave follow-ups.

papers.title: SN 2025dys: A luminous supernova explosion from a partially stripped helium star
papers.result: SN 2025dys reached a peak bolometric luminosity of $L = (8.57\pm 0.41)\times 10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ with early X-ray emission detected at $L_{\rm X} \approx 7.55\times 10^{40}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. Modeling with CSI and radioactive decay requires an ejecta mass $M_{\rm ej} \approx 2.45\text{--}2.69\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, kinetic energy $E_{\rm K} \approx 0.37\text{--}0.46\,\mathrm{foe}$, circumstellar medium mass $M_{\rm CSM} \approx 0.54\text{--}0.76\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, and an optical depth of $\tau_{\rm CSM} = 13$ from early electron-scattering wings.
papers.problem: Unraveling whether the high peak luminosity and spectral evolution of the peculiar transient SN 2025dys are driven by radioactive decay, a central magnetar engine, or shock interaction with a confined, dense circumstellar medium around a stripped-envelope progenitor.
papers.method: Multi-band photometry fitting via MOSFiT testing pure radioactive decay ($s=0, 2$), magnetar engine, and CSI+RD models, combined with early electron-scattering profile modeling using Monte Carlo radiative transfer and Swift-XRT X-ray analysis.
papers.reason: The paper presents comprehensive multi-wavelength observations and light-curve/spectral modeling of SN 2025dys, providing quantitative constraints on circumstellar interaction (CSI) and mass loss around a partially stripped helium star.

papers.title: Long-term variability of the 35-day cycle in Her X-1
papers.result: The 35-day precessional period exhibits a secular decline with $\dot{P}_{35} \approx (-5.04 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$ as measured by RXTE/ASM and MAXI, and piecewise rates of $(-1.3 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$ and $(-4.7 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$ separated by the anomalous low state (ALS) at MJD 51500, matching the theoretical prediction of accretion-driven moment-of-inertia evolution $\dot{P}_{\rm pr}/P_{\rm pr} \approx -(\dot{\Delta I})/\Delta I \sim -\frac{1}{4}(\dot{M}/M_{\rm NS})(P_{\rm pr}/P_*) \sim -2\times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ yielding $\dot{P}_{\rm pr} \sim -6\times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$.
papers.problem: Whether the 35-day super-orbital cycle in Her X-1 is purely governed by chaotic accretion disk precession or paced by a quasi-stable underlying clock mechanism such as neutron star free precession.
papers.method: Multi-mission X-ray light curve analysis (CGRO/BATSE, RXTE/ASM, Swift/BAT, Fermi/GBM, MAXI) spanning over 50 years using sliding-window phase averaging and parabolic $O-C$ phase fitting: $\phi(t) = \phi_0(T_0) + \frac{P_{35} - P_0}{P_0 P_{35}}(t - T_0) + \frac{\dot{P}_{35}}{2 P_{35}^2}(t - T_0)^2$, combined with a biaxial neutron star free precession model governed by $\frac{\dot{P}_{\mathrm{pr}}}{P_{\mathrm{pr}}}=\frac{\dot{P}_{*}}{P_{*}}+\frac{\dot{I}_{3}}{I_{3}}-\frac{\dot{(\Delta I)}}{\Delta I}+(\tan\theta)\dot{\theta}$.
papers.reason: The paper provides an observational and theoretical analysis of the long-term (~50 yr) evolution of the 35-day super-orbital cycle in the X-ray binary Her X-1, demonstrating that neutron star free precession driven by accretion-induced moment of inertia evolution can serve as the underlying clock for warped accretion disk precession.

papers.title: Gamma-Ray Emission from LS 5039: A 30-500 GeV Excess and Phase-Resolved Broadband Spectral Modeling
papers.result: A high-energy spectral excess at $\sim 30$–$500\,\mathrm{GeV}$ is detected at $\sim 7.90\sigma$ significance ($\Delta\mathrm{TS}=72.34$). The broadband lepto-hadronic model improves the spectral fit over purely leptonic models (BIC drops from $93.42$ to $82.62$ in SUPC and from $140.54$ to $136.27$ in INFC), though fast-escaping protons requiring $L_p \sim (1.04\text{--}3.00)\times 10^3 L_{\rm sd}$ create a severe energy budget challenge.
papers.problem: Purely leptonic one-zone intra-binary shock (IBS) models suffer from severe Klein-Nishina suppression and synchrotron cooling, failing to account for the $30$–$500\,\mathrm{GeV}$ excess and HAWC $>100\,\mathrm{TeV}$ ultra-high-energy emission.
papers.method: Fermi-LAT data reduction (0.1–500 GeV, P8R3_SOURCE_V3) with phase-resolved spectral fitting (BPL vs. BPL+LP), combined with numerical modeling of an intra-binary shock governed by momentum ratio $\eta = L_{\rm sd}/(\dot{M}v_w c) \simeq 0.05$ and MCMC spectral fitting using Naima.
papers.reason: This study analyzes 17.3 years of Fermi-LAT data of the gamma-ray binary LS 5039 and investigates particle acceleration in colliding-wind shocks, relevant to high-energy compact object emission and multi-messenger astrophysics.

papers.title: Formation of Micron-sized Presolar Graphite Grains in Low-energy Supernova Ejecta
papers.result: In Ni-free ejecta undergoing matter-dominated adiabatic expansion, the final graphite grain radius scales analytically as $r_{\rm gr,final} \simeq 615\,\mu\mathrm{m}\,(E_{\rm exp}/10^{48}\,\mathrm{erg})^{-3/2}\,(M_{\rm ej}/5\,M_\odot)^{5/2}\,(R_0/10^{12}\,\mathrm{cm})^{-2}\,(X'_{\rm C}/3\times 10^{-3})$, governed by the local key parameter combination $X'_{\rm C}\rho_{2000}\tau_{\rm cool,2000} \propto X'_{\rm C}E_{\rm exp}^{-3/2}M_{\rm ej}^{5/2}R_0^{-2}$. Micron-sized grains ($r_{\rm gr} \gtrsim 1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$) require low explosion energy ($E_{\rm exp} \lesssim 10^{49}\text{--}10^{50}\,\mathrm{erg}$), massive ejecta, and negligible radioactive $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ heating, as $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ heating delays dust condensation until the ejecta expands to much lower densities, suppressing final grain radii below $0.1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$.
papers.problem: Presolar graphite grains extracted from meteorites exhibit supernova isotopic signatures and reach sizes $\gtrsim 1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$, whereas standard core-collapse supernova models ($E_{\rm exp} \sim 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$, $M_{\rm ej} \sim 10\,M_\odot$, $M_{\rm Ni} \sim 0.01\text{--}0.1\,M_\odot$) typically predict graphite grain sizes below $0.1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$.
papers.method: A spherical, uniformly expanding one-zone ejecta dynamics model coupled to an energy equation including radioactive $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}\rightarrow{}^{56}\mathrm{Co}\rightarrow{}^{56}\mathrm{Fe}$ decay heating $\dot{Q}$, $p\,dV$ work, and radiative cooling. Dust formation is calculated using classical homogeneous nucleation theory for carbon monomers and moment equations $dK_j^{(\ell)}/dt$ coupled to key species depletion, with analytical scaling relations derived for the matter-dominated adiabatic limit ($T \propto \rho^{2/3}$) at the reference condensation temperature $T = 2000\,\mathrm{K}$.
papers.reason: The paper investigates the physical conditions required to form micron-sized presolar graphite grains in supernova ejecta, providing key scaling relations linking grain sizes to explosion energy, ejecta mass, progenitor radius, and nickel heating.

papers.title: Nova V1674 Her as a fast magnetic rotator
papers.result: The quiescent X-ray spectrum is consistent with multi-temperature shock emission with a high maximum temperature $kT_{\max} \ge 69\text{ keV}$, yielding a massive white dwarf estimate of $M_{\text{WD}} = 1.26_{-0.56}^{+0.11}\,M_\odot$ (or $\approx 1.35\,M_\odot$).
